newsitem.title: UK: BA cabin crew to vote on strike action.
newsitem.headline: BA cabin crew to vote on strike action.

text.p: Cabin crew at British Airways Plc are to vote on strike action after a long-running pay dispute, said the union representing members of BA's cabin crew on Friday.
The British Airline Stewards and Stewardesses Association, a branch of the Transport and General Workers Union, is balloting 10,000 members over possible strike action.
The vote comes after five month of talks between BA and the union broke down over the failure to agree on BA's proposals for pay restructuring.
The proposed deal would provide crew with higher pensionable pay, in return for efficiencies within the department and lower pay rates for new crew staff.
The result of the ballot will be announced on June 27.
"It follows British Airway's refusal to negotiate with the T&G," said T&G national secretary for civil aviation George Ryde.

A BA spokesman told Reuters, "We believe that their members would not support strike action because what we are proposing is what they have wanted for very many years. ie higher pensionable salaries."
He said that in the event of industrial action, the airline's contingency plans would ensure that British Airways continued to operate.
BA said that it now feels there is little room for any meaningful discussion as it claims that the union first endorsed the pay restructuring proposals but then withdrew shortly after.

BA announced earlier this month that cabin crew union Cabin Crew 89, which represents less than 10 percent of BA's cabin crew, had overwhelmingly voted in favour of proposals that endorsed the airlines' efficiency plans.

This followed on the heels of a decision by BA's World Cargo staff to vote in favour of plans to convert it into a world class freight carrier, which included a two-year pay freeze and loss of 400 jobs from the current work force over the next two years.
BA said both deals would contribute towards its plans to generate one billion pounds of cost savings by the year 2000.
